project.title: Harbor Roast: Fog Line Fall Roast

series_lock.character: roaster seen only as hands or from behind, charcoal wool sweater
series_lock.environment: small dockside roastery, oiled walnut counter, black steel drum roaster, fogged windows
series_lock.lighting: cool fog daylight from windows camera-left, warm practicals behind, deep shadows
series_lock.color_grade: warm dark grade, ground #1C1510, cream #F2E8DA, one #D9822B amber accent, fine grain

shots.subject: one plain stoneware cup of black coffee on the walnut sill of a fogged window, cup in the lower-right third, grey fog in the glass filling the upper two-thirds, no person in frame
shots.rationale: The first frame has to say the season changed before a thumb swipes, so it opens on fog in the glass and one cup; the cup sits low-right so the hook line owns the empty upper frame.

shots.subject: the drum roaster door open and dark beans pouring into the round perforated cooling tray, the stirring arm turning, a thin plume of roast smoke, gloved hands at the tray edge lower-left, the sight glass glowing as the single accent, upper third clear
shots.rationale: The roast arrives as an action, beans dropping out of the drum, which is the moment the brand's motion rule says a cut should land on; the low angle and slow push make one machine in a small room read as the hero.

shots.subject: freshly roasted dark beans heaped in the perforated steel cooling tray, a faint oil sheen on some beans, the stirring arm blade crossing the lower-right, beans filling the lower two-thirds and falling off into shadow in the upper third
shots.rationale: The taste line needs something to sit on that is only the coffee, so this is the one frame with no room and no hands; the beans fall into shadow at the top to give the tasting notes a dark field.

shots.subject: roaster seen from behind at the fogged window, holding a plain stoneware cup in both hands at chest height, back of the head and shoulders soft, figure in the lower-right, upper-left open
shots.rationale: The payoff is the first cup of the new roast, shown from behind so the brand never shows a face selling the coffee; it returns to the fogged window from shot_01 so the film closes the loop it opened.

shots.subject: one plain unprinted kraft paper coffee bag with a folded top standing on the walnut counter beside a small stoneware cup, both in the lower third, the dark roastery soft behind, upper two-thirds dark and clear
shots.rationale: The CTA needs the thing you can buy, a bag, held still for three seconds as the timing rules ask at 15s; the bag is unprinted so the name and the call to order are composited in brand type, never generated.
